final_candidates.decision_summary: Removes the V3/C3 N332-supersite glycan, likely altering neutralization epitopes while preserving core Env folding and replication fitness.
Abolishes the N136 glycan sequon more conservatively than N136S, reducing antibody recognition while lowering local destabilization risk.
Removes a V3 stem glycan, plausibly contributing to antibody escape and likely tolerated for replication.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available and another LLM-only round is unlikely to change the Top-3 glycan-knockout candidates.

history.rationale: Removes the N330/N332-equivalent V3 glycan, likely disrupting PGT121-class antibody binding. Located in a variable surface loop, so replication fitness may be partially retained.
V3/C3 glycan knockout likely to alter neutralization epitopes while preserving core fitness.
Eliminates the N136 glycan in V1 by altering the sequon, likely reducing V1/V2 apex antibody recognition while being a conservative loop substitution.
Thr-to-Ala abolishes the N136 sequon more conservatively than removing Asn; rank above N136S.
Removes a V1/V2 glycan implicated in apex-directed antibody contacts, potentially shifting the local glycan shield without abolishing core folding.
V1/V2 glycan removal plausible but slightly more likely to affect trimer stability than top candidates.
Directly removes the N136 glycan in V1, likely impairing glycan-dependent antibody binding; the loop location suggests partial fitness tolerance.
Direct Asn removal is redundant with T138A and less conservative; lower priority.
Removes a glycan adjacent to the V3 loop, likely altering the V3 glycan supersite recognized by multiple bnAbs while preserving basic Env structure.
V3 stem glycan removal likely contributes to escape and is plausible for fitness.
Removes a V2 loop glycan, potentially modulating V2-dependent antibody epitopes and shifting the glycan shield on a flexible surface region.
V2 glycan knockout may contribute to escape but has moderate fitness uncertainty.
Removes a V4 glycan and may alter the local surface shield, though its contribution to fitness is less certain.
C3-proximal glycan removal is more likely to affect folding/CD4 contact; low confidence not competitive for final top-3.

rejection.reason: C3-proximal glycan removal is more likely to affect folding/CD4 contact; low confidence not competitive for final top-3.

history.rationale: Removes another V4 glycan, potentially contributing to immune escape by reshaping a variable surface loop.
C3-proximal glycan removal has high fitness/folding risk; low confidence not competitive.

rejection.reason: C3-proximal glycan removal has high fitness/folding risk; low confidence not competitive.
